title: Stelvio · Umbrail · Bormio Loop
slogan: Two passes and 87 km, high point 2757 m
story: The Stelvio is the one every rider names, and the numbered hairpins on the Prato side deserve it. Ride it early: by ten the cyclists, campers and coaches turn the top third into a slow-moving queue. The Umbrail descent into Switzerland is the reward - narrower, emptier and far better surfaced than its reputation.

Nothing on this route is higher. At this height the road is a summer one: snow gates can stay shut into June and shut again in October. Next is Prato allo Stelvio, 12 km on and mostly downhill.

title: Transfăgărășan North–South
slogan: Romania's ridge road: tunnels, dam wall and a glacial lake at the top. · out and back
story: Built as a military road across the Făgăraș ridge, the Transfăgărășan spends its best kilometres above the treeline. The northern ramps are the spectacular half; the southern side runs longer and gentler past the Vidraru dam. It is only open in the warm months and the top can shut with no notice, so treat any plan as provisional.

title: Trollstigen · Geiranger Golden Route
slogan: A 268 km loop out of Åndalsnes
story: Trollstigen climbs a near-vertical wall with the Stigfossen falls spilling across it, and the viewing platform at the top looks straight back down the stack. Link it with the Geiranger ferry and Ørnesvingen and you have the most photographed day of riding in Norway. Book nothing tightly - the ferries set the pace.

title: Route des Grandes Alpes · Galibier Stage
slogan: 3 passes in 111 km, topping out at 2642 m
story: The Galibier is the centrepiece of the Route des Grandes Alpes: a long, exposed climb over 2600 m with the Télégraphe as its warm-up. The surface is good, the gradients are steady, and the traffic is mostly other people who came for the same thing. Snow can keep the top shut into June.

title: Great Ocean Road · Apollo Bay Run
slogan: Cliff-edge coast, rainforest curves and the Twelve Apostles. · out and back
story: The coastal section from Torquay to Apollo Bay is the part riders come for: the road runs on a ledge between cliff and surf with bend after bend. Inland through the Otways it turns green and technical. Go midweek - this is one of Australia's busiest tourist roads and the viewpoint car parks fill early.

title: Tail of the Dragon · Cherohala Skyway
slogan: 318 curves in 11 miles, then the empty high road back.
story: Deals Gap is famous for a reason and infamous for another: 318 curves packed into eleven miles, heavily policed, and photographed by professionals at the bends. Ride it once for the story, then take the Cherohala Skyway back - longer, higher, emptier and arguably the better road.

slogan: Atlantic headlands, French Acadian coast and moose country. · out and back
story: The Cabot Trail wraps the Cape Breton Highlands: long climbs onto exposed headlands, then drops to fishing villages. French Mountain and MacKenzie Mountain are the gradients worth planning around. Moose are a genuine hazard at dawn and dusk - this is not a road to ride tired in low light.

title: Grossglockner Hochalpenstrasse
slogan: Austria's showpiece toll road to a glacier viewpoint at 2500 m.
story: The Grossglockner road was built to be ridden slowly and looked at: thirty-six hairpins, a museum at the top and the Pasterze glacier at the end of the Franz-Josefs-Höhe spur. It is a toll road with published opening hours, and the gates close overnight - a late start can leave you locked out.

sections.advice: Along the high section to the Hochtor at 2,504 m, where Salzburg meets Carinthia and the road passes through the summit tunnel. Expect cold air and wind at the top whatever the valley said.

sections.advice: Down the southern side and along the spur to the Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe, the viewpoint over the Grossglockner and the Pasterze glacier. It is a dead end: you ride back the same way to rejoin the road.

sections.advice: Back along the spur and down to Heiligenblut. A long descent on a toll road that is normally open from early May to early November; brakes and gearing matter more than speed here.

scenicChapters.title: Grossglockner Hochalpenstrasse
scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 2428 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance — cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Grossglockner Hochalpenstrasse
scenicChapters.narrative: 37 km that neither climbs nor drops much. The road settles into the ground rather than fighting it. This is where a day makes up time without anyone trying. Third and fourth, and very little else.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

title: Amalfi Coast · Ravello Balcony
slogan: A 91 km loop out of Sorrento
story: The SS163 is barely wide enough for the buses that use it, which is exactly why a motorcycle is the right vehicle here. Ride it at first light and it is one of the great coast roads; ride it at noon in August and it is a car park with a view. Ravello above it is the quiet alternative.

waypoints.name: Sorrento
waypoints.advice: Sorrento is where the day begins. Next is Positano, 18 km on.

waypoints.name: Positano
waypoints.advice: Positano comes up 18 km in. Next is Amalfi, 18 km on.

waypoints.name: Amalfi
waypoints.advice: A break here at 36 km, with 55 km after it. Next is Ravello, 19 km on and climbing 355 m.

waypoints.name: Ravello
waypoints.advice: Ravello, about halfway at 365 m. The road climbs 355 m over the 19 km before it, steadily. Reckon on about 2 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Next is Salerno, 18 km on and mostly downhill.

waypoints.name: Salerno
waypoints.advice: Salerno sits at 73 km, late in the day. You lose 355 m on the way down to it, steadily. Next is back to Sorrento, 18 km on.

waypoints.name: back to Sorrento
waypoints.advice: The route ends here after 91 km.

scenicChapters.title: Amalfi Coast Road
scenicChapters.narrative: Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast. For 2 km this is Amalfi Coast Road, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it.
